clinicalPearls: A type II collagenopathy caused by COL2A1 mutations, usually autosomal dominant, with many cases arising de novo.
Presents at birth with disproportionate short-trunk short stature, a barrel-shaped chest and a short neck.
Radiographs show platyspondyly with delayed, irregular ossification of the vertebral bodies, femoral heads, pubis and knee epiphyses.
Odontoid hypoplasia and ligamentous laxity predispose to atlantoaxial instability and cervical myelopathy; assess the cervical spine before any anaesthetic or surgery.
High myopia carries a lifelong risk of retinal detachment and warrants regular ophthalmology review.
Cleft palate, sensorineural hearing loss and muscular hypotonia may accompany the skeletal features.
Coxa vara, a waddling gait, exaggerated lumbar lordosis and progressive kyphoscoliosis are characteristic.
Intelligence and facial appearance are typically normal, although the midface may look flat.
reference.pathophysiology: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita results from heterozygous mutations in COL2A1, which encodes the alpha-1 chain of type II collagen, the predominant collagen of hyaline cartilage, the vitreous of the eye and the nucleus pulposus. Most mutations act through a dominant-negative mechanism, so structurally abnormal collagen trimers disrupt the cartilage extracellular matrix and disorganise the growth plate. Impaired endochondral ossification produces the delayed and irregular epiphyseal and vertebral ossification that defines the disorder, while the same defective collagen in ocular, auditory and other connective tissues explains the myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration and hearing loss. The condition lies on a phenotypic spectrum of type II collagenopathies extending from lethal achondrogenesis type II and hypochondrogenesis, through Kniest dysplasia, to the milder Stickler syndrome.
additionalDifferentials: Kniest dysplasia and other type II collagenopathies
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey with attention to the spine, pelvis and long-bone epiphyses
Flexion-extension cervical spine radiographs and MRI to assess atlantoaxial stability and cord compression
Formal ophthalmological assessment including retinal examination for myopia and detachment risk
Assessment of the palate for clefting and, where relevant, evaluation for sleep-disordered breathing
redFlags: New limb weakness, spasticity, gait deterioration or sphincter disturbance suggesting cervical cord compression
Sudden visual loss, floaters or flashing lights indicating retinal detachment
Respiratory compromise in infancy from a small thorax or cervical instability
Rapidly progressive scoliosis with cardiorespiratory impact
reference.prognosis: Intelligence and life expectancy are usually normal, but morbidity arises from cervical instability, early osteoarthritis of the hips and spine, progressive scoliosis, and visual and hearing complications; many affected individuals require joint replacement or spinal surgery in adult life.
pitfalls: Failing to screen for atlantoaxial instability before general anaesthesia or surgery, risking catastrophic cord injury
Misdiagnosing the condition as a mucopolysaccharidosis such as Morquio syndrome
Overlooking progressive myopia and retinal detachment, leading to preventable visual loss
Attributing the hypotonia to a primary neuromuscular disorder rather than to the dysplasia
management: No disease-specific drug therapy; management is supportive and orthopaedic with structured surveillance
Cervical spine assessment with flexion-extension imaging and MRI for odontoid hypoplasia and atlantoaxial instability, with fusion or stabilisation and precautions before any anaesthetic or surgery
Orthopaedic management of scoliosis and early hip and spinal osteoarthritis, often requiring joint replacement or spinal surgery in adult life
Ophthalmology surveillance for high myopia and retinal detachment
Audiometry and management of sensorineural hearing loss, with assessment and repair of cleft palate
Evaluate for sleep-disordered breathing and support muscular hypotonia with physiotherapy
Multidisciplinary clinical genetics, orthopaedic, ophthalmology and ENT care
Genetic counselling given autosomal dominant COL2A1 inheritance, noting that many cases arise de novo
